messages:
carmen: FYI during int4 bringup for reranker-lite we see a reproducible MRR drop on the very short-query cohort (len<=5). ndcg@10 stable, mrr@10 ~0.06 down vs fp16.
reza: what's the eval split and sample size? are candidates identical ordering between runs?
carmen: holdout split, ~2.5k queries. candidate pool is same source but ordering seems to differ sometimes. pasted quick stats: fp16: ndcg@10=0.825 mrr@10=0.642; int4: ndcg@10=0.824 mrr@10=0.583.
kai: big delta. could be tokenizer/truncation or priming interaction. short queries are sensitive to small score perturbations.
carmen: we observed that when priming is enabled the top1 flips more often under int4. without priming mrr gap shrinks to ~0.01.
reza: so priming shifts low-margin logits and quantization amplifies tie flips. action items: 1) add a short-query priming guard (skip priming if query_len<=5) 2) deterministic tie-breaker in postprocess (stable sort by doc_uid) 3) add paired-perquery top1-flip metric to bringup harness.
kai: also capture raw logits for top-5 for a sample of 200 short queries to inspect score margins. store as artifact in the bringup job.
eval-bot: triggered eval job 1815001235 (short-slice smoke) with priming disabled and stable-sort enabled.
carmen: quick results: priming-off: mrr@10=0.635 ndcg@10=0.824 ; priming-on+stable-sort: mrr@10=0.629 ndcg@10=0.824 ; priming-on (no stable-sort): mrr@10=0.583 ndcg@10=0.824.
reza: good signal. stable-sort reduces variance but priming still nudges scores. guard + stable-sort seems safest.
kai: let's add a CI bringup check: fail if top1-flip-rate > 1.5% on short slice or mrr delta > 0.02 vs fp16. also add a note in model-catalog: "reranker-lite int4: avoid priming for queries <=5 tokens; stable-sort enabled by default".
carmen: opening PR with three small changes + bringup test. linking logs and raw-logit artifacts in the PR.
eval-bot: created ticket ML-2310 and attached eval artifacts.
reza: when you open the PR tag runtime and infra reviewers, priming lives in both candidate generator and ranker paths. need end-to-end check.
carmen: will do. thanks everyone.
